rationale:
The reporting hierarchy is conveyed ONLY by margin-left on flat

elements, with no list nesting. A media query zeroes the indentation at 320px, flattening five levels into one column, so the reader can no longer tell which team sits under which division. Meaningful structure is lost on reflow.
citation: G224: "There can be instances where indentation of text is considered important to the presentation and understandability of the text content. If the indentations were to be removed, then meaning or functionality could suffer."

rationale: A media query forces the <pre> to wrap and collapses leading whitespace at 320px, destroying the block structure of the code. The nesting that shows scope (loops inside conditionals) is no longer perceivable, which G224 warns can break understanding or even function.
citation: G224: "maintaining indentations can be important to help understand code patterns, if not even necessary for the code to function."

rationale: Sub-clause scope (which 2.x belongs under clause 2) is shown only by padding-left on flat divs. At 320px the padding is removed, so 2.1 and 2.2 no longer visibly sit under clause 2 and the scope of each sub-clause becomes ambiguous, changing the legal reading.
citation: G224: "If the indentations were to be removed, then meaning or functionality could suffer."

rationale: Reply depth in a threaded discussion is conveyed only by margin-left on flat comment divs. At 320px the margins are removed, so a reply-to-a-reply becomes visually identical to a top-level comment and the conversation's structure (who answered whom) is lost.
citation: G224: indentation that is "important to the presentation and understandability" must be preserved on reflow.

rationale: The poem's deliberate indentation encodes alternating voices (the visual shape of the verse). Removing the indent at 320px erases the cue that distinguishes the voices, changing the intended reading of the poem.
citation: G224: indentation "considered important to the presentation and understandability of the text content" — if removed, "meaning or functionality could suffer."

rationale: A list that looks nested is actually flat divs with a leading glyph and margin-left for depth. At 320px the indentation collapses, so sub-steps no longer read as belonging to their parent step, and there is no real list nesting to fall back on.
citation: G224: removing meaningful indentation causes "meaning or functionality" to suffer.

rationale: A directory tree's nesting (which file lives in which folder) is shown purely by left padding on flat rows. At 320px the padding is removed and every path looks top-level, so a nested file is indistinguishable from a root file. The structural meaning is lost.
citation: G224: indentation important to understandability must survive reflow; if removed, "meaning or functionality could suffer."

rationale: Although real <ul> nesting carries the structure in the DOM, a media query at 320px zeroes padding/margin and sets list-style:none, so the visual indentation that distinguished sub-topics from topics is gone. The presented structure G224 is about preserving is destroyed for sighted users even though the markup nesting survives.
citation: G224 is about preserving the PRESENTED indentation on reflow: "the indentation was maintained, but as much text was made visible within the viewport as possible." Here it was not maintained.

rationale: An email-style quote chain shows each level of quoting by nested indentation. At 320px the indentation and border are removed, so the reader can no longer tell which quoted text replies to which — the meaningful conversational nesting is erased.
citation: G224: "If the indentations were to be removed, then meaning or functionality could suffer."

rationale: In a structured proof, indentation marks which lines form a sub-derivation under an assumption. Removing the indent at 320px makes it ambiguous where the assumption's scope ends, changing the logical reading of the proof.
citation: G224: indentation "important to the presentation and understandability" — if removed, meaning suffers.

rationale:
Terms and definitions are flat

s distinguished only by indentation (definitions indented under their term). At 320px the indent is removed, so terms and definitions run together and the reader cannot tell where one entry ends and the next begins.
citation: G224: removing meaningful indentation causes "meaning or functionality" to suffer.

rationale: A first-line text-indent is a purely typographic convention for prose paragraphs and carries no structural meaning. Whether present or removed at 320px, the reading is identical, so collapsing this gratuitous indentation is fine.
citation: G224 distinguishes indentation that is "important to the presentation and understandability" from decorative indentation; only the former must be preserved.

rationale: The syllabus uses real nested <ul> and the indentation is maintained (reduced, not removed) at 320px, so the meaningful structure remains perceivable. This is exactly G224's approach to reflow.
citation: G224: "the indentation was maintained, but as much text was made visible within the viewport as possible."

exception: valid: code <pre> keeps white-space:pre and scrolls horizontally to preserve indentation
rationale: The same code as the positive case-02 but here indentation is maintained at 320px: the <pre> keeps white-space:pre and scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping, so the code structure survives. This is G224's intent realized with the SC 1.4.10 2D exception for the code block.
citation: G224: "maintaining indentations can be important to help understand code patterns"; SC 1.4.10 exception permits 2D scrolling for content that requires it 'for usage or meaning'.

rationale: The pull-quote's large left margin is an aesthetic offset, not a structural cue; it conveys no nesting or hierarchy. Removing it at 320px loses no meaning because the quote is still clearly a quote via its styling and <blockquote> element.
citation: G224: only indentation "important to the presentation and understandability" must be preserved; decorative offsets may collapse.

rationale: The hierarchy is carried by explicit section numbering (1, 1.1, 2.1) and real heading levels, not by indentation, so the decorative indent may collapse at 320px with no loss because the structure is encoded in the visible numbers and headings.
citation: G224: where structure is conveyed by means other than indentation, collapsing the indentation does not cause meaning to suffer.

rationale: A single-level list whose only indentation is the conventional bullet offset. There is no nesting, so reducing the offset at 320px changes nothing structural.
citation: G224 concerns indentation that encodes meaning; a flat list's bullet offset does not, so collapsing it is harmless.

rationale: A nested ordered list where sub-steps are genuinely under their parent step; the indentation is reduced but kept at 320px and the ordered-list numbering reinforces the structure, so the nesting remains perceivable on reflow.
citation: G224: "the indentation was maintained, but as much text was made visible within the viewport as possible."

rationale: A hanging indent is a typographic convention for reference lists; each reference is an independent, self-contained entry with no nesting. Flattening the hanging indent at 320px loses no meaning.
citation: G224 distinguishes meaningful from decorative indentation; a hanging indent on independent references is decorative.

rationale: Threaded replies are indented, but each reply also states its depth in text ('reply to Ada', 'reply to Ben') and the indentation is reduced rather than removed at 320px, so the structure remains clear both visually and textually after reflow.
citation: G224: indentation maintained on reflow (and reinforced by a redundant textual cue) preserves the meaning.

rationale: The 'Note:' aside is indented purely to set it off visually; it is a standalone, non-nested remark whose meaning is carried by the 'Note:' label and the <aside> styling, not the indent. Collapsing the indent at 320px is harmless.
citation: G224: only indentation important to understandability must be preserved; a decorative aside offset may collapse.

rationale: Indented lines have their indentation removed at 320px, but whether the indent encodes meaningful structure (sub-points of the line above) or is a decorative offset is genuinely ambiguous from the markup alone. Deciding requires understanding the author's intent / the content's meaning, which a deterministic runner cannot resolve, so it should flag for human review.
citation: G224 hinges on whether indentation is "important to the presentation and understandability" — a content-meaning judgment that is undeterminable here from structure alone.
